brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Organism metaphor with orbiting particles is a fresh, memorable framing for system load that hints at a living system
Restrained black/amber palette and clean sans-serif headers create a coherent dashboard mood with adequate hierarchy
dominant_weaknesses: Both organisms look nearly identical despite different stress states — no visible pulse-rate, color-shift, or distortion to signal critical health
Massive empty canvas with two centered blobs wastes spatial budget; numerals feel small relative to the orbital halo and vast negative space
Status bar says 'Critical' but visual language stays calm amber — semantic mismatch undermines the entire breathing/stressed concept
fix_priorities: Differentiate stress states visually: faster orbits, redshift of color, jitter, and tighter rings when usage exceeds thresholds
Tie color to severity (amber→red gradient) so 74% CPU at 78°C reads as visibly alarmed, not ambient
Densify layout: add sparkline history, per-core organisms, or process list to justify the screen real estate
Strengthen typographic contrast — larger central readout, smaller ring, weight variation between label and value
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept (organisms as metaphor) outpaces visceral payoff and behavioral signal — the design tells you it's critical but never makes you feel or react to it.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially — the organism shape exists, but without differential motion/color between healthy and stressed states, the core brief of 'breathes steady vs pulses fast' is unfulfilled in the static frame.
